es: Seguir un debate de vecinos y extraer posturas, propuestas y acciones con responsable y plazo.

teaching.en: Carlos is in favour of the new bike lane, whereas Mia is opposed to it, so the group has not yet reached a consensus on the proposal.
teaching.es: Carlos está a favor del nuevo carril bici, mientras que Mia se opone, así que el grupo aún no ha alcanzado un consenso sobre la propuesta.
teaching.explanationEs: Be in favour of / be opposed to + nombre declara una postura; consensus es el acuerdo de todos sin votar.
segments: Carlos is in favour of the new bike lane, whereas Mia is opposed to
it, so the group has not yet reached a consensus on the proposal.
teaching.audioText: Carlos is in favour of the new bike lane, whereas Mia is opposed to it, so the group has not yet reached a consensus on the proposal.

teaching.en: Leo put forward the proposal, and his position is clear, but I am afraid I cannot agree, because it would cost far more than the council has promised.
teaching.es: Leo presentó la propuesta y su postura está clara, pero me temo que no puedo estar de acuerdo, porque costaría mucho más de lo que el ayuntamiento ha prometido.
teaching.explanationEs: Put forward: presentar una propuesta ante el grupo. I am afraid I cannot agree es un desacuerdo educado; position resume lo que alguien defiende.
segments: Leo put forward the proposal, and his position is clear, but I am afraid
I cannot agree, because it would cost far more than the council has promised.
teaching.audioText: Leo put forward the proposal, and his position is clear, but I am afraid I cannot agree, because it would cost far more than the council has promised.

teaching.en: Although Tom voiced his dissent, the discussion was constructive: everybody wanted safer streets, and the only sticking point was the cost.
teaching.es: Aunque Tom expresó su desacuerdo, el debate fue constructivo: todos querían calles más seguras y el único obstáculo era el coste.
teaching.explanationEs: Voice dissent: expresar desacuerdo. Sticking point: el obstáculo concreto que bloquea un acuerdo.
segments: Although Tom voiced his dissent, the discussion was constructive: everybody wanted
safer streets, and the only sticking point was the cost.
teaching.audioText: Although Tom voiced his dissent, the discussion was constructive: everybody wanted safer streets, and the only sticking point was the cost.

teaching.en: I take your point, Leo, but the real obstacle is not the idea itself; it is finding a volunteer willing to manage the scheme.
teaching.es: Entiendo lo que dices, Leo, pero el verdadero obstáculo no es la idea, sino encontrar a un voluntario dispuesto a gestionar el proyecto.
teaching.explanationEs: I take your point reconoce lo dicho antes de discrepar; volunteer es quien se ofrece sin que se lo pidan.
segments: I take your point, Leo, but the real obstacle is not the
idea itself; it is finding a volunteer willing to manage the scheme.
teaching.audioText: I take your point, Leo, but the real obstacle is not the idea itself; it is finding a volunteer willing to manage the scheme.

teaching.en: Whoever agrees to be responsible for an action must also be given a deadline, otherwise nobody can check whether it has been done.
teaching.es: Quien acepta encargarse de una acción debe recibir también un plazo; si no, nadie puede comprobar si se ha cumplido.
teaching.explanationEs: Be responsible for + nombre asigna la tarea; action y deadline completan el acuerdo: qué, quién y cuándo.
segments: Whoever agrees to be responsible for an action must also be given
a deadline, otherwise nobody can check whether it has been done.
teaching.audioText: Whoever agrees to be responsible for an action must also be given a deadline, otherwise nobody can check whether it has been done.

teaching.en: At the end, the chair repeats each action point, names the person who will carry it out and states the date by which it must be finished.
teaching.es: Al final, la presidencia repite cada punto de acción, nombra a la persona que lo llevará a cabo y indica la fecha límite.
teaching.explanationEs: Cada acción acordada lleva un responsable y una fecha; la presidencia los repite para dejarlos claros.
segments: At the end, the chair repeats each action point, names the person who will
carry it out and states the date by which it must be finished.
teaching.audioText: At the end, the chair repeats each action point, names the person who will carry it out and states the date by which it must be finished.

prompt.es: Lee la intervención de Carlos. ¿Cuál es exactamente su postura?

choices.text: He backs it fully, whatever the council decides about the signs.
He rejects it, unless the signs are made much smaller.
He backs it, but only if the council funds the signs.

feedback.es: Carlos apoya el carril con una condición («only if»): que el ayuntamiento pague los carteles. Sin ella votaría en contra.

hint.es: Fíjate en la condición que introduce only if: sin ella cambia su voto.

origin.text: Carlos: I am in favour of the bike lane, but only if the council agrees to pay for the new signs. Otherwise, I am afraid I would have to vote against it.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me temo que me opongo al plan: quita la mitad del estacionamiento.»

feedback.es: Be opposed to + nombre declara una postura en contra; la preposición que acompaña a opposed es siempre to.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo de postura contraria que se construye con to.

origin.text: Mia does not want the lane on her street. At the meeting she says, «I am afraid I am ___ to the plan, because it removes half of the parking.»

prompt.es: Ordena: «La decisión final se alcanzó por consenso y nadie expresó su desacuerdo.»

answer.text: The final decision was reached by consensus and nobody voiced dissent

feedback.es: Reach a decision by consensus: decidir sin votar; voice dissent: expresar abiertamente el desacuerdo.

hint.es: Empieza por el sujeto The final decision y acaba con la expresión del desacuerdo.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué propone Leo para desbloquear el debate.

choices.text: A three-month trial followed by a review.
A total ban on parking in the street.
A vote delayed until the council replies.

feedback.es: Leo sugiere una prueba de tres meses con revisión posterior. La prohibición de estacionar es el temor de Mia, y la carta al ayuntamiento es una acción de Sara.

origin.audio: Last Thursday, the residents' association met to discuss turning Oak Street into a cycle route. Carlos argued strongly in favour, pointing out that two children had been hurt on that street last year. Mia accepted the risk but insisted that removing the parking would hurt the elderly residents, who depend on their cars. Leo suggested a compromise: a trial of three months, after which the association would review the results. Everybody accepted it, although Mia said she would wait for the results before changing her mind. Sara will write to the council by Friday.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué postura mantiene Mia al final de la reunión.

choices.text: She has dropped her objection now that a trial is planned.
She accepts the trial but has not changed her mind yet.
She rejects the trial and will keep opposing the route.

feedback.es: Mia acepta la prueba pero dice que esperará a ver los resultados antes de cambiar de opinión: su postura sigue siendo cautelosa; ni ha retirado su objeción ni rechaza la prueba.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del debate con su función en la tabla de la reunión.

pairs: Mia insisted that the parking must stay

pairs.es: Postura contraria, con un motivo concreto
Propuesta intermedia para desbloquear el debate

pairs: Sara will write to the council by Friday

feedback.es: Una postura defiende algo con un motivo, una propuesta ofrece una salida, una acción lleva responsable y plazo, y un acuerdo recoge lo que todos aceptan.

prompt.es: Escucha el resumen de la presidencia. ¿En qué coinciden Leo y Sara?

choices.text: Both want the market to be held only once a month.
Both fear that the market will cause noise and litter.
Both welcome the market, though Sara would cap the stalls.

feedback.es: Leo apoya el mercado y Sara comparte su opinión, aunque quiere limitar los puestos. El ruido y la suciedad preocupan a Tom, no a ellos.

origin.audio: The chair summed up the debate on the new market. Leo is in favour, because it would bring customers to the high street. Sara shares his view but wants a limit on the number of stalls. Tom is worried about noise and litter and thinks the market should be held only once a month. Nobody is completely against the idea, so the chair suggested a three-month trial on the first Saturday of each month. Carlos agreed to contact the sellers by the end of the week.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez. ¿Qué se deduce de la postura de Tom?

choices.text: He is not against the market but wants to limit its impact.
He objects to the market in principle and wants it cancelled.
He supports the market fully but wants it held more often.

feedback.es: Tom no rechaza el mercado: pide solo una vez al mes por el ruido y la suciedad. Quiere reducir el impacto, no impedirlo.

origin.audio: The chair summed up the debate on the new market. Leo is in favour, because it would bring customers to the high street. Sara shares his view but wants a limit on the number of stalls. Tom is worried about noise and litter and thinks the market should be held only once a month. Nobody is completely against the idea, so the chair suggested a three-month trial on the first Saturday of each month. Carlos agreed to contact the sellers by the end of the week.

prompt.es: Según el acta, ¿quién hará la siguiente gestión y para cuándo?

choices.text: Tom, who must explain the staffing costs by 14 May.
Carlos, who must obtain the figures by 14 May.
Sara, who must state her position by the next meeting.

feedback.es: El acta asigna la acción a Carlos con fecha: pedir las cifras a la biblioteca antes del 14 de mayo. Tom y Sara no tienen acción asignada.

origin.text: Item 3. Proposal: keep the library open later on Saturdays. In favour: Mia, Leo. Against: Tom (staffing costs). Not sure: Sara. Action: Carlos will ask the library for the figures by 14 May. The vote will take place at the next meeting.

prompt.es: Completa: «La presidencia le recordó que el plazo era el viernes.»

feedback.es: Deadline es la fecha límite de una acción; en el acta va siempre junto a la persona responsable.

origin.text: Nobody wanted to be left with the whole job. In the end Sara agreed to take charge of the letter, and the chair reminded her that the ___ was Friday.

prompt.es: ¿Qué deja entrever Mia con su comentario sobre las plazas para bicicletas?

choices.text: That she likes the scheme but dislikes its location.
That she will accept the scheme as soon as the council confirms the money.
That her real worry is who will look after the racks later.

feedback.es: Mia no discute la idea en sí, sino quién se hará cargo cuando se acabe el dinero: su preocupación real es el mantenimiento a largo plazo.

origin.text: Mia: I take your point, Leo, but I am afraid I cannot agree. The scheme sounds sensible on paper, yet nobody has explained who will look after the bike racks once the council's money runs out.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué se deduce del resumen de la presidencia.

choices.text: That a small trial is possible even though the group is divided.
That the vote has been postponed until a majority appears.
That the opposing members have agreed to stop objecting.

feedback.es: Hay cuatro a favor, dos en contra y una indecisa, pero la presidencia ve suficiente acuerdo para empezar con algo pequeño.

origin.audio: Well, to sum up where we are: four members favour a pilot scheme, two are against it, and one has not yet made up her mind. There is no consensus, but there is enough agreement to try something small. Leo will draft the wording, Mia will check it with the school, and both will report back at the next meeting.

prompt.es: Completa: «Como nadie quería escribir la carta, Sara decidió ofrecerse.»

feedback.es: Volunteer to + verbo base: ofrecerse por iniciativa propia; Sara no recibe el encargo, lo asume.

origin.text: Nobody wanted to write the letter to the council, so in the end Sara decided to ___ to do it herself.
